What are the poles of a magnet?

explain.say: Hold two bar magnets. Sometimes they snap together with a click. Turn one round, and they wriggle away as if they are shy! Every magnet has two ends, called poles: a north pole and a south pole. Let's sort what happens when poles meet.

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: a bar magnet. Can you see the north pole and the south pole? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.

draw.text: Attract or repel: what magnet poles do

explain.say: See Attract lighting up? Attract means pull together. When a north pole meets a south pole, the magnets pull together and snap. Opposite poles attract. Can you remember which poles are friends?

groups.label: Repel

explain.say: Look at this magnet on the board, being pulled towards a south pole. See the arrow? The pull gets stronger as the magnets get closer, so they speed up at the end and click! Have you felt that tug in your fingers?
Now Repel glows. Repel means push away. North meets north, or south meets south, and the magnets push each other apart. Same poles repel. Can you push two north poles together? It is hard!

explain.say: See this magnet pushed away, sliding off to the right? You can even make a magnet float above another by repelling. Fantastic work! Wow fact: the whole Earth is a giant magnet, and a compass needle is a tiny magnet that swings to point north.

faq.q: What are the poles of a magnet?
faq.a: The poles are the two ends of a magnet, where its pull is strongest. One is called the north pole and the other the south pole.
asks: What is a north pole on a magnet?

faq.q: Why do magnets push each other away?
faq.a: When two of the same poles face each other, north and north or south and south, the magnets repel, which means push apart. Opposite poles attract.
Attract means pull towards. Opposite poles of magnets, north and south, attract each other, and magnets attract iron and steel objects.
A compass needle is a small, light magnet that can spin. The Earth acts like a giant magnet, so the needle's north pole swings round to point roughly north.
asks: Why does a compass point north?

faq.q: Does a magnet pull harder when it is closer?
faq.a: Yes. A magnet's pull or push is much stronger close up and gets weaker quickly as you move it away.
asks: Why do magnets snap at the end?

facts: Like magnetic poles repel and unlike poles attract.
A compass works because the Earth has its own magnetic field.

quiz.say: You put the north pole of one magnet near the north pole of another. What happens?
quiz.why: Same poles repel, so they push each other apart.

wrong.2: Magnets close together always push or pull each other.

quiz.say: Why does a compass needle point north?
quiz.show: A compass needle points north because…

options.show: It is a magnet and Earth is magnetic
options.say: It is a magnet and Earth is magnetic

options.show: It is heavier at one end
options.say: It is heavier at one end

quiz.why: The needle is a tiny magnet pulled into line by the Earth's magnetism.

wrong.1: A compass works inside a closed case with no wind.
wrong.2: Weight does not decide the direction; magnetism does.
